records.finding: The legacy initialize/response/initialized sequence negotiates version and capabilities; an unsupported returned version should cause disconnection. The text correctly limits the local adapter to its tested legacy revision.

Initialization is the first exchange. The client sends its supported version
and capabilities; the server returns its version and capabilities; the client
then sends \texttt{notifications/initialized}. A server that cannot use the
requested version can return another supported version. If the client cannot
use the returned version, the specification says it should disconnect.
Normal operations must respect the negotiated capabilities~\citep{v12_mcp_legacy_lifecycle}. The local adapter restricts negotiation to its
tested legacy revision. Receiving a response to initialization is therefore
insufficient: the client must inspect what version was actually selected.

records.finding: StructuredContent plus serialized JSON text is the backward-compatibility recommendation; output-schema validation is appropriate. Unknown tool protocol errors and isError execution/input errors are distinct; scientific refusal is explicitly the local service meaning, not a third protocol error category.

The server returns the canonical response in \texttt{structuredContent} and
as serialized JSON in a text-content block, following the inspected tool
specification's compatibility recommendation. A client that supports
structured content should validate it against the output schema and retain
the scientific fields. A client using the text copy must parse that JSON,
rather than ask a model to invent a convenient summary of it. A discrepancy
between representations is an interface defect to investigate~\citep{v12_mcp_legacy_tools,v12_in_runtime}.

There are three distinct negative-result layers. An unknown tool is a
JSON-RPC protocol error, with the recorded adapter returning code $-32602$.
A tool execution or input-validation failure is a tool result with
\tex

ror, with the recorded adapter returning code $-32602$.
A tool execution or input-validation failure is a tool result with
\texttt{isError=true}. A scientifically unsupported or refused request can
be a successful tool execution whose canonical disposition explains that
no requested effect was computed. The inspected legacy tool specification
distinguishes the first two layers; the third is the causal service's own
typed scientific meaning. A client which interprets
\texttt{isError=false} as ``causal conclusion accepted'' discards that meaning~\citep{v12_mcp_legacy_tools,exec13_i2_examples}.
